title: A repeat FTC refund is conditioned on prior payment acceptance while second-check cashing and debt recovery remain unobserved
source_unit: FTC ACRO Services debt-relief refund program and repeat-payment route
geography: United States consumers affected by ACRO Services debt-relief practices

denominator.unit: people reported as having accepted the first refund and receiving a second-round check

first_round_total.unit: U.S. dollars or more reported for the first round

recipient_condition.unit: administrative eligibility condition for the second round

second_check_receipt.unit: missing individual delivery, cashing, returned-check, reissue, debt-balance, and account-correction outcomes

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the current official FTC ACRO Services refund page, with the project event ledger retained as the compact reproduction layer. The first-payment acceptance condition is kept separate from second-check delivery or cashing.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not provide individual amounts, the total harmed population, first-payment timing, second-check cashing, original debt balance, residual fees, or household recovery. A recipient-conditioned repeat payment cannot be converted into a recovery rate for all harmed consumers.
observations.subgroup: People who accepted the first ACRO refund and were selected for the second-round check; the record does not expose why other consumers were not included or any socioeconomic subgroup outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prior acceptance makes the second-round group more reachable than an unconditioned population, but it can also exclude people who never received, could not access, or could not cash the first payment.

related_sources.claim: The FTC refund index lists ACRO Services as an official refund program and provides the program route.
The FTC case materials provide enforcement context for the ACRO debt-relief refund program.

boundary: This record follows a recipient-conditioned repeat-refund route from prior payment acceptance to reported second-check dispatch. It does not establish second-payment receipt, cashing, debt correction, adequacy, household recovery, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the official FTC refund page; direct command-line access to the publisher page was rate-limited during canonical promotion.
